title: 1958 up to 60 ft. in height spruce trees used in grid work
description: Spruce timber gridwork was used to build the arches. Floyd Page stated, “50-60 foot limbed spruce timbers with the bark still on, were steam hammered down into the pan. Dennis Clendenning was responsible for running the crane, putting the steam hammer on, and pounding all day, never shutting it off, for two shifts. Sandy Hawkes made the steam using an air-cooled, flash-burning iron-horse engine fueled by stove oil. It made steam in 1.5 minutes and sat on a drag and piped steam through a hose to the hammer.”
